title: Brakes & Air Systems
whatItIs: Check the brakes every day: air builds up and the warning works, there are no leaks, and the service and parking brakes work on both tractor and trailer.

keyFacts.text: Every part of every braking system MUST be maintained in good and efficient working order and properly adjusted.
Trailers with EBS MUST be connected with an ISO 7638 ABS/EBS lead. Without it, the trailer EBS won't work.

keyFacts: The service brake should operate both the tractor and the trailer brakes.
Defective brakes at a roadside check can mean a £100 fine and 3 penalty points.

visual.caption: Brake checks on the daily walkaround

items.title: Air build-up
items.text: Air builds up correctly, the warning system works, no air leaks.

items.title: Service brake
items.text: Works tractor and trailer brakes. Pedal: no excess side play, tread intact.

items.title: Parking brakes
items.text: Check the tractor parking brake and the trailer parking brake both work.

items.title: Brake lines and couplings
items.text: Couplings clean and in the right place. No leaks, damage or wear.

items.title: ISO 7638 lead
items.text: Inspect for damage and connect correctly. It runs trailer ABS/EBS.

items.title: Warning lights
items.text: ABS and EBS warning lights work correctly.

a.label: Service brake
points: The footbrake: works tractor and trailer brakes
Stop lamps on when applied, off when released

b.label: Parking brake
points: Check tractor and trailer parking brakes
MUST be applied before leaving the vehicle

onTheTest.question: A trailer fitted with EBS isn't connected with the ISO 7638 lead. What's the result?
options: Nothing: the air lines are enough
onTheTest.why: Without the ISO lead the trailer EBS won't function. The trailer must not be used until the fault is put right.

onTheTest.question: You must brake in an emergency in a vehicle with ABS. What does The Highway Code advise?
options: Brake firmly and keep the pressure on
onTheTest.why: Apply the footbrake firmly and don't release the pressure until you've slowed to the speed you want. ABS should let you keep steering control.

traps: ABS helps you steer while braking, but don't assume it stops you in a shorter distance.
After driving through deep water, test your brakes gently at the first safe opportunity.
Coasting removes engine braking and makes you use the footbrake more, which can reduce its effectiveness.
